_voice: Informal "tú", standard written Irish (An Caighdeán Oifigiúil).
_style: Write standard Irish (An Caighdeán Oifigiúil) and always address the user with informal singular “tú/do” (“Do ghiúmar”, “Seol”); use “sibh/bhur” or, more warmly, “an bheirt agaibh” only when speaking to both partners together (“bhur dturas”, “an bheirt agaibh”). The other person is “do pháirtí” (gender-neutral noun; note lenition after “do”: do pháirtí, do chuid); never fear/bean chéile, buachaill/cailín, and never use “sé/sí” for the partner: repeat “do pháirtí”, use the name placeholder, or rephrase (“Tá do pháirtí réidh”, not “Tá sí réidh”). Avoid gendered adjectives about the user. The name placeholder %@ is never lenited, eclipsed, prefixed (no h-/t-/n-) or put in the vocative/genitive: rephrase so it stands in the nominative (“Sheol %@ síol chugat”, “Ó %@”, not “ó Sheán” style mutation or “a %@”); never add “a” before it as a vocative. Initial mutations after possessives, articles and prepositions are mandatory for normal words (mo chrann, ár gcrann, sa ghairdín, ar an gcrann). Quote marks: “ ” outer, ‘ ’ inner; ellipsis is one character …; no space before ? ! : ; ; em dash — as in the source; keep “ · ”, \n, emoji and placeholders exactly. Numbers: Irish/English digits, decimal point “.”, thousands separator “,”; dates follow the locale formatter (e.g. 14 Samhain 2026), month names lowercase-initial only inside sentences if the formatter does so; time 24-hour is fine. Plural categories are one, two, few (3–6), many (7–10), other (0, 11+): Irish keeps the noun singular after a number and mutates it by category — one: “%lld chrann”, two: “%lld chrann” (lenition), few: “%lld chrann” (lenition), many: “%lld gcrann” (eclipsis), other: “%lld crann”; lá stays “lá” throughout except many: “%lld lá” (vowel-initial nouns take n- in many: “%lld n-uair”). Fill all five categories every time; where a mutation reads awkwardly, use a counter phrase such as “Laethanta: %lld”. Buttons and actions use the imperative singular verb (Sábháil, Seol, Uiscigh, Plandáil, Bain triail eile as); titles, tabs and buttons use sentence case (only the first word capitalised) except proper names: Coupley, Premium, IS (for AI). Script: Latin alphabet with síneadh fada (á é í ó ú) always written; never drop accents. Tone warm, light, natural spoken Irish, never cheesy or word-for-word.
